title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: conversation orchestration with natural language playbooks
summary: The roadmap facts, opt-in configuration, routing behaviour and consumption-based billing are supported. The credit exemption is now documented without being described as planned, and the control path and checklist coverage need minor clarification.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 Contact Center administrators define conversation orchestration using natural language playbooks.
claims.quote: Administrators define the logic by using natural-language playbooks, and conversation orchestration handles the execution.

claims.claim: Playbooks act on conversations while they wait in queues.
claims.quote: Conversation waiting in queue | Triggers orchestration while a conversation is waiting in a queue.

claims.claim: A playbook consists of a trigger event and conditions and actions.
claims.quote: A playbook consists of a trigger event and a set of conditions and actions to run when the trigger event occurs.

claims.claim: Playbooks are configured through guided templates.
claims.quote: Configure playbooks for each scenario through guided templates that keep instructions focused and reliable.

claims.claim: The configuration page documents four supported scenario categories.
claims.quote: Dynamic prioritization; Overflow handling; Assign to a preferred expert or previously engaged representative; Bullseye routing through user groups

claims.claim: Dynamic prioritisation can increase or reset conversation priority.
claims.quote: Automatically increase or reset conversation priority based on wait time, queue transfers, or queue consults

claims.claim: Playbooks support overflow handling when queue conditions change.
claims.quote: Configure real-time overflow actions when queue conditions change

claims.claim: Playbooks support assignment to a preferred or previously engaged representative.
claims.quote: Route conversations to a preferred expert mapped to the contact or to a representative who previously interacted with the customer

claims.claim: Bullseye routing progressively expands eligible representatives through user groups.
claims.quote: Start assignment with a targeted Level 0 user group, then progressively expand to additional user groups as wait time increases.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft tells administrators to test, monitor and revise runtime behaviour.
claims.quote: Administrators should test and monitor runtime behavior and revise the playbook if orchestration doesn't work as intended.

claims.claim: Neither the notice nor the configuration page says routing changes for queues without an active playbook.
claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration feature toggle enable disable setting; read configuration page, Responsible AI FAQ and MC1536059. No automatic routing change for unconfigured queues stated.

claims.claim: Conditions use customer context variables such as CustomerTier, Is VIP Customer, Preferred Language, Customer Region and Account Type.
claims.quote: Choose from available context variables such as CustomerTier, Is VIP Customer, Preferred Language, Customer Region, or Account Type.

claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration language model data receives privacy processing; read configuration page and Responsible AI FAQ. They describe playbook conversion but not the complete model-input payload or processing location.

claims.quote: System administrator or Omnichannel administrator role.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the feature should not be used for employment decisions including compensation, rewards or seniority.
claims.quote: This feature is not intended for use in making—and should not be used to make—decisions that affect the employment of an employee or group of employees, including compensation, rewards, seniority

claims.claim: Customers are responsible for lawful use, adequate notification and obtaining end-user consent where applicable law requires it.

claims.claim: Published playbooks run relevant actions automatically, without approval for each run.

claims.claim: A playbook action can keep a conversation unassigned.
claims.quote: Keep the conversation unassigned | Keeps the conversation unassigned in its current queue as the configured treatment.

claims.claim: Deleting an active playbook immediately stops orchestration for the corresponding queue.
claims.quote: If you delete an active playbook, conversation orchestration stops for the corresponding queue immediately.

claims.claim: Multiple active playbooks for the same scenario and queue conflict and cannot be published.
claims.quote: You can't have multiple active playbooks for the same scenario and the same queue. This configuration creates a conflict that prevents publishing.

claims.claim: Dynamic prioritisation does not apply to queues with custom prioritisation rules.
claims.quote: It doesn't apply to queues with custom prioritization rules.

claims.quote: Required fields; Range validation; Duplicate conditions; Conflicting conditions; Cross-playbook conflicts

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Licensing is mixed: specific Dynamics 365 licensing requirements apply alongside consumption-based Copilot Credits billing.
claims.quote: Specific licensing requirements apply to configure and use conversation orchestration in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Learn more in Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide. ... Set up consumption-based billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature page points to the Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide but does not name the required licence itself.
claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration licensing Contact Center licence credits included; read configuration prerequisites and billing page. The feature prerequisites refer to the Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide without naming a licence.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature page describes publishing a playbook as the credit-consuming event, rather than runtime conversation processing.
claims.quote: Conversation orchestration consumes Copilot credits only when you publish a playbook
claims.fix: Qualify the summary and cost rationale with 'except qualifying one-branch, wait-time-only playbooks without context variables', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/manage-overflow#understand-copilot-credit-usage. The feature page gives the general rule, but the cited overflow page now documents this exception without a planned qualifier.

claims.claim: A published playbook can process any number of customer conversations without extra Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: After you publish, the playbook can process any number of customer conversations without consuming extra Copilot credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Saving a draft or enabling conversation orchestration does not consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: When you save the playbook as a draft or enable conversation orchestration, it doesn't consume Copilot credits.

claims.claim: MC1536059 also says credits are consumed on publication and not during runtime.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are consumed when administrators publish playbooks. The feature does not consume Copilot credits during runtime execution.

claims.claim: Upgrading legacy wait-time in-queue overflow can use a credit-exempt playbook.
claims.quote: An upgraded or newly created playbook doesn't use Copilot credits if it meets all of these conditions:
claims.fix: Replace the heading '**Planned exemption.**' with '**Credit exemption.**' and replace its opening sentence with 'The overflow documentation describes a credit exemption for upgraded or newly created playbooks that meet all the conditions below.' The current page does not call the exemption planned; keep the existing conditions and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/manage-overflow#understand-copilot-credit-usage.

claims.claim: The credit exemption requires exactly one branch, only the wait-time-in-queue-exceeds condition and no context variables.
claims.quote: It has one branch only. The branch contains the waiting time in queue exceeds condition only. The playbook doesn't use context variables.

claims.claim: Other conditions, multiple branches or any context variables cause playbooks to use Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Playbooks use Copilot credits if they include other conditions, multiple branches, or any context variables.

claims.claim: Publishing fails when the required credits are unavailable.
claims.quote: Publishing fails if the required credits aren't available.

claims.quote: For pay-as-you-go, use Microsoft Cost Management in the Azure portal to view detailed usage and adjust spending limits (budgets) to free up more capacity.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited pages do not state a number of Copilot Credits per playbook publish or a separate repeat-publication rate.
claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration Copilot credits publish rate licensing; read configuration, billing, overflow and Responsible AI pages. No per-publish credit number or separate Save & publish rate stated.

claims.claim: The prerequisites require unified routing enabled for the environment.
claims.quote: Unified routing enabled for your environment. At least one queue and workstream is configured for voice or messaging channels. A voice or messaging channel is configured.

claims.claim: The printed Copilot Service admin center path reaches the playbook queue and channel configuration pane.
claims.quote: go to Customer support > Conversation Orchestration. ... select Prompt gallery. ... select a scenario category, and then select a playbook template. ... Select Queues > Edit to open the queues pane.
claims.fix: Keep the path and add to controls[0].note: 'In Queues > Edit, select Channel: Voice or Messaging and Apply to: All queues, List of queues, or All queues except. Return to the playbook editor, select Save to save a draft, and select Publish to activate the playbook.' The printed path reaches the right pane but not publication. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/contact-center/administer/configure-conversation-orchestration.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No cited reference documents an automation operation that publishes a playbook with the configured queue and channel scope.
claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration publish Web API msdyn_ccuserprompt msdyn_channel; read CC User Prompt reference and configuration page. Record CRUD and writable columns exist, but no publish-operation semantics or queue-list payload format is documented.

claims.claim: The Responsible AI FAQ says administrators can disable the feature toggle to turn off conversation orchestration.
claims.quote: Administrators of Dynamics 365 Contact Center can delete any saved or published playbooks, disable the feature toggle to turn off the feature

claims.claim: Active-playbook edits use Save & publish to save and immediately publish changes.
claims.quote: For active playbooks: Select Save & publish to save and immediately publish your changes. The Save button is disabled for active playbooks ... If you cancel, the playbook reverts to the last published version.

claims.claim: All controls the governance checklist asks readers to configure or monitor have corresponding table rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Set up consumption-based billing'; 'Limit the System administrator and Omnichannel administrator roles'; 'Monitor playbook behaviour with the diagnostics custom query'. Table: 'Which queues and channels a playbook applies to, and whether it is published'.
claims.fix: Record the table-coverage gap for billing set-up, administrator-role restriction, custom-prioritisation inventory and diagnostics monitoring. Do not add rows or unverified paths and automation as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Power Platform pay-as-you-go requires an Azure subscription.
